subject: Request: bridge letter and interim controls evidence for SOC 2 procurement - Fintegrity
messages:
From: Alex Porter <aporter@fintegrity.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Huang <claire@auditsolutions.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: bridge letter and interim controls evidence for SOC 2 (Fintegrity procurement)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. As we discussed with procurement, Fintegrity is evaluating Redwood for a payments integration and needs a SOC 2 Type II attestation covering the period ending 2023-12-31. The audit report you provided looks good, but our security and legal teams want a bridge/coverage letter to confirm controls between the report period end and our anticipated go-live (we're targeting 2024-09-15). In addition to the bridge letter, we need a few interim artifacts to complete our assessment:

- A short statement that lists exactly which Trust Services Criteria are covered by the bridge (e.g., CC1-CC7) and whether any control changes have occurred since 2023-12-31.
- A current network diagram showing boundary components (DMZ, VPCs, third-party integrations).
- Evidence of patching and vulnerability management (summary of last 90 days).
- Evidence of recent backup tests and DR runbook ownership.
- The contact info for your auditor so we can confirm the bridge letter scope if needed.

Could you please provide a draft bridge letter (Word/PDF) and the artifacts above by EOD next Thursday (2024-08-08)? If your auditor can produce an attestation or memo, that would speed our legal review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement has a hard calendar on this.

Thanks,
Alex Porter
Head of Vendor Risk | Fintegrity Inc
aporter@fintegrity.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: procurement-req-summary.xlsx (referenced)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2024 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bridge letter and interim controls evidence for SOC 2 (Fintegrity procurement)

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list and the timeline. We can meet the 2024-08-08 target for a first pass. Looping in Neha (compliance lead) and Priyom (security ops) to assemble the evidence and draft a bridge letter.

Quick notes / asks from our side:
- Our SOC 2 Type II cover period ends 2023-12-31; the bridge will explicitly cover the period from 2024-01-01 through 2024-09-15 (or until you indicate go-live). If you'd prefer a shorter interim window we can adjust.
- Are you expecting auditor-signed language or is a company-signed management assertion sufficient for procurement? That will determine next steps for Claire.

Neha / Priyom: please see Alex's ask below; we should draft a management bridge letter and prepare the following artifacts: network diagram (current), 90-day vuln management summary, backup/DR test summary, change log for control-affecting changes since 2023-12-31. I'll request the auditor confirmation in parallel.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Attachment: none

Thanks Alex — adding detail on our planned deliverables below. Priyom and I will collate the evidence and attach as separate PDFs.

Planned deliverables by 2024-08-08 (first pass):
- Bridge letter (management assertion) in Word: bridge_letter_finreq_draft.docx (attached). Draft will:
  - State scope: management assertion covering CC1-CC7 for infrastructure, logical access, change mgmt, backup/DR, monitoring.
  - Period covered: 2024-01-01 through 2024-09-15 (editable).
  - Statement on changes: we will list control changes above a materiality threshold; currently there are two non-control-affecting vendor updates and one documented policy revision (change logging updated 2024-03-12).
- SOC 2 report (provided earlier): SOC2_Type_II_20231231.pdf (we'll reattach).
- Network boundary diagram: network_diagram_v2.pdf (attached).
- Vulnerability management summary: vuln_summary_90d.pdf (will attach).
- Backup / DR summary and runbook owner confirmation: dr_test_summary.pdf (will attach).
- Control change log: control_changes_2024.csv (will attach).

Claire — can you confirm if an auditor-signed memorandum is required for procurement, or whether a company-signed bridge + auditor contact is sufficient? If you are able to provide a short auditor memo that references the original SOC 2 report and scope, that would be ideal.

I'll assemble the attachments and aim to have everything in a zipped packet by COB 2024-08-08.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments (to follow): bridge_letter_finreq_draft.docx, network_diagram_v2.pdf, SOC2_Type_II_20231231.pdf

From: Claire Huang <claire@auditsolutions.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@fintegrity.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Aug 2024 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bridge letter and interim controls evidence for SOC 2 (Fintegrity procurement)

Rafael / Neha / Alex — thanks for the context. I reviewed the draft bridge letter (bridge_letter_finreq_draft.docx) and provided a short auditor memorandum and a signed bridge letter (signed_bridge_letter_20240802.pdf) that ties back to the SOC 2 Type II report dated 2023-12-31. High-level notes:

- Auditor memo: confirms auditor-reviewed procedures limited to inquiry and inspection of provided artifacts; it is not a full re-audit. Language is conservative: references original report date, lists the control areas we reviewed (logical access, change management, backups, vulnerability mgmt) and the artifacts we inspected.
- Bridge letter: management assertion + auditor acknowledgement appended; covers interim period 2024-01-01 through 2024-09-15.
- No material control changes were identified in the artifacts we reviewed. The policy revision noted (change logging) is administrative and does not weaken control design.

Next steps for procurement: Claire suggests Fintegrity legal accept the bridge as a supplemental attestation; if they require a signed auditor opinion beyond a memorandum, that would require an expanded engagement and additional fee.

I've attached: signed_bridge_letter_20240802.pdf (signed bridge letter), auditor_memo_20240802.pdf (auditor memorandum), and a short redline to the draft (bridge_letter_redline.docx).

Claire Huang, CPA
Audit Solutions LLP
claire@auditsolutions.com
+1 (212) 555-0146

Attachments: signed_bridge_letter_20240802.pdf, auditor_memo_20240802.pdf, bridge_letter_redline.docx
